content.title: We appreciate the reviewers for their comments.
content.comment: We agree with their general opinion on the lack of clarity and experiments including thorough ablation study and parametric study. There are several misunderstandings in the reviewer’s comments, but they also imply that the current version of the manuscript is quite not ready for publication. Hence, we decided to withdraw the manuscript without further rebuttals. We again thank the reviewers for their comments.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper aims to improve multi-agent coordination with several improvements in key areas to increase sample efficiency and encourage coordination. The method is based primarily on an episodic MARL framework (Zheng et al. 2021), with the following changes:
1) Storing joint strategies rather than joint actions in episodic memory, and using the memory with a hard $l_2$ distance cutoff rather than a soft tradeoff parameter
2) Decomposing group rewards to individual rewards by comparing against the best joint trajectories in episodic memory, and using these individual rewards in a novel TD target that correctly utilizes the episodic memory.
3) Adding an intrinsic reward that maximizes the mutual information between agent trajectories and strategy trajectories,
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
* The related works section is thorough and addresses relationships to all of the components in the framework. 
* The framework is generally well motivated and logically derived from existing works, while simultaneously introducing several novel ideas. 

Weaknesses:
* The paper could use additional proofreading, as it is difficult to understand in it's current state. There are several minor typos and formatting errors, and some explanations could be made more clear. Some obvious spelling fixes are below, but in many cases I'm not certain what the authors are trying to convey. 
* SIMA also requires tuning of one hyperparameter relating to episodic control, $\delta$, which serves a similar role to $\lambda$ used in EMC and other prior works. I would like to see some ablations of this value, as well as the final value selected. In general I would like to see more ablations, as there are many independent changes made in this paper and the effects of these changes should be disentangled.  Examples would be the effect of decomposing group rewards or the effects of removing either the TD target or the coordination incentive alone. Explicitly stating additional hyperparameter settings would also improve the reproducibility of the experiments. 
* SIMA does not convincingly exhibit improved performance compared to the baselines, especially considering the complexity of the framework. It performs well in some tasks, but significantly worse on others, compared to conceptually much simpler baselines. 

Questions:
* Preliminary/Definition 1: $\pi_z$ is defined on $T \times A_z \equiv (\Omega \times A \times A_z)$. I'm quite confused by the meaning of this equation, as it's different from the usual definition of an RL policy. 
* How much computational power is required for each training run? 

Minor:
* Introduction/Final Paragraph: "StrarCraft" -> "StarCraft"
* Related Works/Episodic Control: "this estimation on true values requires sample efficiency" doesn't seem to be the right statement. 
* Preliminary/Definition 1: Defines $Q^s_i$ in terms of Eq. 25, which is found in the appendix. A brief explanation of the equation in the main body of the paper would be helpful. 
* Section 4.1/Construction of an Episodic Buffer: "paring" -> "pairing"
* $\delta$ is used to denote both the limit of similar state representations in Eq. 1 and the Dirac delta function, these should have separate notation. 
* Appendix C "StraCraft" -> "StarCraft"
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Quality:
The experimental results are not convincing in terms of improvement over existing methods. The paper has several minor typos and formatting errors. 

Clarity:
There are multiple places where grammatical issues and poor phrasing make the paper difficult to understand. 

Originality:
The paper combines several existing ideas - episodic control, hierarchical RL, VDN mixing networks - in an original way, while also introducing a novel TD target, episodic control mechanism, curiosity incentive, and coordination objective.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper combines several existing methods with novel components in a complex framework. Unfortunately, the experimental results are not convincing, especially given the complexity of the method, and the general quality of the paper is lacking. I would not recommend this paper for acceptance as is, although I would be open to changing my score in light of additional experiments and clarifications.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors propose SIMA, an algorithm based on a novel formulation of the TD to increase the sample efficiency in multiagent RL. This TD target includes a strategy mixer which enables automatic switching between episodic control and a conventional Q-learning, based on episodic context. In addition, each agent needs to behave similarly according to its strategy trajectory for coordinated behaviors among agents and coherent evaluation of a group’s joint strategies.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros
------
* An interesting set of ideas in a highly complex space (multiagent RL)

Cons
------
* Profoundly unclear formulation and definitions. Are strategies essentially policies? Transforms from policies to policies? Something else? It's unclear why one would need to complicate the framework with the unclear distinction between policies and strategies to begin with - this is not to say there isn't a good reason, just that as the paper is written and presented now, it's hard to understand it, if it does exist.

* It's entirely unclear how hierarchy factors into anything in the proposed framework, and much closer analogues (options, for instance) aren't properly considered or discussed. The notion of distribution matching to encourage coordinated behavior is also strongly reminiscent of other threads, such as imitation learning, which is not discussed in the paper.

*  It's not clear whether Proposition 1 implies convergence. 

* The results don't seem particularly conclusive.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Mostly discussed under "cons" in the Strength and Weaknesses. In general, the paper isn't particularly well organized or written. A substantial revision for clarity is necessary, particularly in sections 3-4.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, it seems there are interesting ideas in here, but I had a very hard time teasing them out from the manuscript. As such, I fear it isn't quite ready in the sense that the presentation needs to be polished substantially (both in terms of methodology and in terms of results) in order to be useful to the general ML community.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper studies the problem of cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning through the lens of hierarchical RL. In particular, it proposes Strategy Identification Multi-Agent RL (SIMA). First, SIMA uses episodic memory for sample efficiency, i.e., memorizing the highest return and corresponding joint strategy for each state, derives an individual reward for each agent from this memory, and trains a strategy selector shared between all agents. It also encourages coordination through an intrinsic bonus based on the mutual information between the policy’s generated trajectories and the selected strategies. In the experimental evaluation, SIMA is compared to an array of prior methods, including QMIX, QPLEX, EMC, CDS, and RODE on the StarCraft II benchmark.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
- The paper tackles a challenging problem, which is cooperative multi-agent RL, and makes some progress on some of the SMAC maps.
- The paper provides a strong empirical analysis of the proposed method, including an ablative study and qualitative analysis of the algorithm.

Weaknesses:
- The proposed method SIMA is quite complicated. While there are ablative experiments to study the importance of each component, some missing details make it difficult to understand. For example, what is VND? Additionally, is the episodic control component ablated in Section 5.2? The curiosity-based bonus is only briefly mentioned in Section 4, but evidently, it seems to play a big role in the improved performance of SIMA.
- While SIMA improves upon prior methods on some of the maps, it also performs worse in others. The advantages of SIMA are not very clear. A discussion of what is learned by each method in the “MMM2” and “corridor” maps would be useful to help understand why SIMA learns slower. I would also recommend including an averaged curve that aggregates the performance across different maps to see overall trends.
- The evaluation tasks are somewhat narrow, compared to prior works, which also study Google Research Football in experiments.
- The clarity of the paper could be significantly improved. There are currently many grammatical errors and missing details.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity/Quality: Some suggestions/questions I have are
- “subset of action spaces” → “subset of the action space”
- “introduces a coordinated Strategy Identification Multi-Agent reinforcement learning (MARL) with episodic memory, called SIMA” → 
"introduces Strategy Identification Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (SIMA)”
- “achived” → “achieved”
- “keeping the best returns and corresponding to the best joint strategies for given states” → “keeping the best returns and corresponding best joint strategy for each state”
- What is VND in Section 5.2? Is this VDN from Sunehag et al?

Novelty: This work combines several existing techniques, including hierarchical RL, episodic control, intrinsic bonuses based on mutual information and on curiosity.

Reproducibility: The experiments section and appendices provide a lot of hyperparameter details about the algorithm and environment. However, the algorithm is quite complicated, so I would recommend including an algorithm box with pseudo-code or open sourcing the code used.
content.summary_of_the_review: While the paper tackles a challenging problem in multi-agent reinforcement learning, the proposed method is pretty complicated with many different components and does not seem to provide a clear advantage over prior methods. The current version of the paper could also be written clearer. For these reasons, I am recommending to reject the paper.

content.title: Coordinated Strategy Identification Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
content.TL;DR: We present a framework which expedites and stabilizes learning of a hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning via episodic memory, while achieving coordinated behaviors among agents with a novel theoretic regularization.
content.abstract: An agent's strategy can be considered as a subset of action spaces, specialized in certain goals. This paper introduces a coordinated Strategy Identification Multi-Agent reinforcement learning (MARL) with episodic memory, called SIMA. SIMA derives a new temporal difference (TD) target to increase the sample efficiency. The efficiency is achived by keeping the best returns and corresponding to the best joint strategies for given states. This TD target with an additive strategy mixer automatically switches between an episodic control and a conventional Q-learning according to the existence of similar memories. In addition, each agent needs to behave similarly according to its strategy trajectory for coordinated behaviors among agents and coherent evaluation of a group's joint strategies. To this end, SIMA introduces a theoretical regularization for action policies to maximize the mutual information between an agent’s trajectory and its specified strategy. We demonstrate its significant performance improvement on the StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge benchmark.
